---
title: "How to cite"
---

## Cite MetaVidence

If MetaVidence produced results you are publishing, cite it like this:

> Costa Filho VO (2026). MetaVidence: no-code meta-analysis in the browser and
> in R. Version 0.1.0. https://metavidence.com

In BibTeX:

```bibtex
@Manual{metavidence,
  title   = {MetaVidence: no-code meta-analysis in the browser and in R},
  author  = {Valbert Oliveira Costa Filho},
  year    = {2026},
  note    = {R package version 0.1.0},
  url     = {https://metavidence.com}
}
```

## Cite the analysis packages too

MetaVidence does not do the maths itself. It calls
[meta](https://cran.r-project.org/package=meta),
[metafor](https://cran.r-project.org/package=metafor),
[netmeta](https://cran.r-project.org/package=netmeta) and
[mada](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mada), and those packages implement
the models. Cite the ones your analysis used, and record each version.

In R, `citation("meta")` gives the exact wording for each. Which ones apply
depends on the module:

| Module | Packages behind it |
|---|---|
| Binary, continuous, pre-calculated, single-arm | meta, and metafor for meta-regression |
| Network meta-analysis | netmeta |
| Diagnostic test accuracy | mada, and meta for the forest plots |
